eyebrow: open() and with — the safe way
code:
with open("yellow_tripdata_2024-01.csv", "r") as f:
    first_line = f.readline()
    print(first_line)
caption: with is a context manager — the file closes automatically, even if an error happens inside.

code:
with open("yellow_tripdata_2024-01.csv", "r") as f:
    header = f.readline()
    for line in f:
        columns = line.strip().split(",")
        fare_amount = columns[10]
        print(fare_amount)
caption: One line at a time — never loads the whole file into memory. A manual version of Lesson 22's real parsing.

code:
with open("cleaned_fares.txt", "w") as f:
    for fare in [14.50, 9.75, 22.00]:
        f.write(str(fare) + "\n")

# "w" overwrites entirely. "a" would append instead.
caption: Chapter 4's PySpark .write() (Lesson 60) is built on this exact open-write-close idea, at cluster scale.
